title: GCL 2026, Day 5: Gambits beat Kings, Pipers defeat Mumba Masters as race to the final heats up
summary: Table toppers FYERS American Gambits added to the misery of Triveni Continental Kings by inflicting yet another defeat on the two-time champions to maintain their advantage over defending champions Alpine APL Pipers at the top of the standings in the Global Chess League (GCL), a joint initiative of Tech Mahindra and FIDE, in Bengaluru on Wednesday. The Pipers had temporarily taken the top spot after beating CheQ Mumba Masters 11-6 in the opening match, but the Gambits ended the day ahead of the defending champions with a better game points score after beating the Continental Kings by a score of 8-5 with the white pieces. In the day’s other matches, Ganges Grandmasters registered a 15-3 victory over Triveni Continental Kings, while Mumba Masters suffered a double heartbreak as they also lost 6-11 against PBG Alaskan Knights. FYERS American Gambits, Alpine APL Pipers and Ganges Grandmasters have now won four matches but the Gambits have played one round more than their closest challengers. Let’s take a closer look at today’s matches: Alpine APL Pipers vs. CheQ Mumba Masters: 11-6 The Pipers were in total control on most boards with the white pieces against the Mumba Masters. World no. 1 Magnus Carlsen played a solid game to beat Maxime Vachier-Lagrave while Anish Giri on the second board grabbed the initiative against M Pranesh early on and never let it go. Volodar Murzin then assured the Pipers their fourth win in six matches as he forced Bardiya Daneshvar to resign after 52 moves. Harika Dronavalli’s win over Divya Deshmukh was the only silver lining for the Mumba Masters in that match. Triveni Continental Kings vs. Ganges Grandmasters: 3-15 Ganges Grandmasters also then completed a double over Triveni Continental Kings, this time dominating the match with black pieces. When the match started, Kings appeared well prepared for the battle with White and eager to continue their revival after a disastrous start. But Ganges Grandmasters’ Polina Shuvalova, who now has five wins from six games, turned the tables on Zhu Jiner to score four points, while Luke Leon Mendonca then cashed in on the error by Pranav V to win the clash on the prodigy board. Stavroula Tsolakidou then put the result beyond doubt by beating former Women’s World Champion Alexandra Kosteniuk in a 63-move mini marathon to set the final score of the match. Mumba Masters vs. PBG Alaskan Knights: 6-11 Mumba Masters had the chance to take the top spot by beating PBG Alaskan Knights with the white pieces and they looked on course till the dying minutes of the match. However Carissa Yip, who had a winning position, lost on time against Nino Batsiashvili and Abhimanyu Mishra put behind him the heartbreaking loss of Tuesday to beat Bardiya Daneshvar to secure his team victory and also pick the Player of the Match award. FYERS American Gambits vs. Triveni Continental Kings: 8-5 In the last match of the day, the Candidates 2026 winner, Javokhir Sindarov, convincingly defeated Alireza Firouzja on the icon board. This crucial win tipped the balance in the Gambits’ favor as the games on all other boards ended in draws. As things stand after Day 5 three teams are on 12 match points: the Gambits have 60 game points from seven matches; second-placed Alpine APL Pipers have 58 game points from six matches while Ganges Grandmasters have 55 game points from six matches. Standings after Day 5 Schedule for Thursday, September 10: 3.30 PM: Alpine APL Pipers vs Ganges Grandmasters5.00 PM: CheQ Mumba Masters vs Triveni Continental Kings6.30 PM: Alpine APL Pipers vs PBG Alaskan Knights8.00 PM: Ganges Grandmasters vs FYERS American Gambits About the Global Chess League The Global Chess League (GCL), a joint initiative between Tech Mahindra and FIDE, is the world’s first and largest official franchise league of its kind. The league brings together leading chess players from across the globe in a unique joint team format, with six players representing each franchise across Icons, Superstar Men, Superstar Women and Prodigies. Men and women compete together on the same team, with every board carrying equal value towards the team’s result. GCL has previously staged seasons in Dubai, London, and Mumbai and returns to India for Season 4 in Bengaluru. GCL official website: https://globalchessleague.com/

title: Every Lesson Counts: FIDE Summit on chess in education comes to Samarkand this September
summary: Leaders in education, policy and chess research to gather during the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad The International Chess Federation (FIDE) will host the FIDE Summit on Chess in Education 2026 on 24 September at Silk Road by Minyoun in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, held alongside the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad and Congress. The Summit is a centrepiece event of the 2026 Year of Chess in Education, and organizers are inviting educators, policymakers, researchers and chess-in-education innovators from around the world to register now to secure their place. Themed “Every Lesson Counts,” the Summit brings together voices from across the global chess-in-education movement to examine where the field stands today and where it is headed next – from long-established national programmes to emerging grassroots initiatives and new partnerships with higher education. The day will be hosted by Simon Bélanger, a videographer, actor and chess content creator known to audiences as @simonplayschess. Following a lunch break, Part II (14:00–15:30) turns to a series of shorter, dynamic panel discussions tracing the past, present and future of chess in education: reflections on established national programmes, the challenges facing emerging pilot initiatives, and the road ahead as higher-education institutions and nonprofit organizations come on board as partners. After a coffee break, the day shifts gears for Part III (16:00–18:00), a closing block of six longer, in-depth Education Innovation Lectures that each take a deep dive into a single theme: chess as a tool for refugee and conflict-affected communities, the journey of FIDE’s own chess-in-education programming, making chess engaging and enjoyable for every child, how chess builds learning and community connections across the globe, the results of a new Chess in Education Global Survey, and chess’s impact beyond the tournament hall. To support participants from around the world, the Summit will offer real-time voice translation in 64 languages; attendees are asked to bring their own headphones. Registration is required for all visitors wishing to attend in person. Register now: https://edu-summit2026.fide.com/ FIDE Summit on Chess in Education schedule (PDF) Participants who need an official invitation letter, for example, to support a visa application, should contact Rita Atkins, Secretary of the FIDE Chess in Education Commission, at edu.secretary@fide.com.  Every lesson counts. Every child can benefit. Join FIDE in Samarkand this September to help shape the future of chess in education.
